title: Static and dynamic context
caption: Static is set up before the shift; dynamic context can be fetched during it. You can limit sources and review what arrives: both land on the same bench.

folder.thing: The folder of the current job
folder.name: Project folder

dynamic-means-loaded-at-run-time.header: Dynamic means loaded at run time
dynamic-means-loaded-at-run-time.description: agents can keep lightweight identifiers such as file paths and links, then use tools to load selected data into context at run time instead of loading everything up front [1]. The available sources depend on the agent's setup; people can limit access and review retrieved material.

anthropic-effective-context-engineering.title: Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents

before-the-shift.title: Before the shift
before-the-shift.script: Static context is everything you set up before the work starts. Picture the bench before the shift: the instruction sheet, the standing rules and the first work order. For an agent that means memory files, system prompts and your initial prompt.

during-the-shift.title: During the shift
during-the-shift.script: Dynamic context is information fetched during the work. In our example, a worker fetches parts, contacts a supplier or opens the current job folder. An agent may retrieve material through tools while it works. You can limit which sources it can reach and review what it retrieves; it does not mean you have to supervise every step.

why-it-matters.title: Why it matters
why-it-matters.script: Why does the difference matter? Both kinds of context can influence the work. The AI may not distinguish the sheet you wrote from material retrieved along the way, so think about what it can access. You can review retrieved material and the result without watching every step.
